title: Molecular Spectroscopy Lab Station
description: The user operates a virtual spectroscopy workstation where the SunglassesKhronos model represents UV-protective spectroscopy goggles and the SpecularSilkPouf represents a reactive chemical sample on an analysis pad. The user must calibrate the spectrometer wavelength, adjust sample exposure, run absorption scans, and identify the compound by matching spectral peaks.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive molecular spectroscopy lab. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader. Position the SunglassesKhronos model at (0, 1.8, -1) as UV-protective spectroscopy goggles mounted on a stand. Position the SpecularSilkPouf at (0, 0.8, 0) on a flat platform mesh representing the sample analysis stage. Add a dark lab environment with a PBR metallic workbench (BoxGeometry), ambient light intensity 0.15, and a focused SpotLight above the sample. Create an HTML overlay control panel on the right side with these interactive steps: (1) A wavelength slider from 200nm to 800nm that changes the SpotLight color from violet through the visible spectrum to red in real-time, also tinting the SpecularSilkPouf material emissive property to simulate fluorescence. (2) An exposure intensity slider (0-100%) controlling SpotLight intensity from 0 to 5. (3) A 'Rotate Sample' button that animates the SpecularSilkPouf 90 degrees on Y-axis per click, requiring 4 orientations to be scanned. (4) A 'Scan' button that, when pressed at each orientation, records the current wavelength and intensity as a data point and draws it on a 2D canvas graph overlay showing an absorption spectrum. (5) A 'Toggle Goggles' button that animates the SunglassesKhronos model down over the camera position to apply a post-processing tint (change scene background and add a semi-transparent colored plane in front of the camera) simulating UV-filter viewing mode. (6) A dropdown to select the identified compound from 4 choices after collecting all 4 scan points. (7) A 'Submit Analysis' button that validates all 4 scans were taken at different orientations, wavelength was between 350-550nm for at least 2 scans, intensity was above 40% for at least one scan, and a compound was selected. Display pass/fail feedback. Use OrbitControls for camera navigation. The camera starts at (3, 2.5, 3) looking at origin.
